answer: Tiered collateral bonding mitigates Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock funds into a stepped staking terrace before transacting. At the dawn of each epoch, smart contracts audit these deposits, stemming the tide of zero-cost automated clones. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of locking scarce capital and forfeiting liquidity for every forged node. A key limitation is that wealthy adversaries can afford massive deposits, marginalizing underfunded honest agents.
